exposure: general movements assessment (fidgety movements and Motor Optimality Score, Revised)
cohort: 30 term-born infants with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) were included.
finding: The assessment of fidgety movements (FMs) and Motor Optimality Score-Revised (MOS-R) demonstrated good predictive value for future neurodevelopmental outcomes, with absent FMs significantly correlating with lower motor and mental developmental quotients and a higher risk of cerebral palsy.
